title: Reliability ramp and handoff matrix — cross-team SLO adoption plan
content:
Purpose
To provide a minimally prescriptive, operationally focused plan for ramping SLO-backed reliability controls across product teams and formally handing day-to-day ownership to team-level on-call and platform squads. This doc pairs a timeboxed ramp calendar with a one-page handoff matrix per service and clear acceptance criteria for go/no-go.

Scope
- Applies to all customer-facing HTTP/gRPC services and core inference control planes that are in production and tagged for SLO coverage in FY26.
- Excludes experimental feature branches and ad-hoc data pipelines (those will adopt a simplified monitoring checklist).

Objectives (measurable)
1) 90% of prioritized services have SLOs defined, instrumented, and visible in the team dashboard by end of Q1 2026.
2) 80% of those services complete a formal handoff (runbook + on-call playbook + postmortem process) to owning product teams within 6 weeks of instrumentation.
3) Reduce mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for P1 incidents by 30% in ramp cohort teams within two quarters of handoff.

High-level approach
- Cohort-based ramping: adopt teams in small cohorts (4–6 services per cohort) for focused enablement and quicker feedback.
- “Instrument → Validate → Handoff” pipeline: instrumentation work by infra/SRE, validation with product/engineering, then handoff with runbook acceptance and on-call rehearsals.
- Lightweight governance: weekly SLO sync + monthly readiness review.

Stakeholders and Roles
- Program Lead: Maya Chen (SRE) — manages cadence, artifacts, and readiness reviews.
- Instrumentation Engineers: Platform infra engineers — implement metrics, alerts, and dashboards.
- Product Service Owners: Product/AE engineers — accept runbooks and take on rota.
- Observability SME: Priya Nair — validates dashboards and alert thresholds.
- Release & Ops Coordinator: Tom Alvarez — schedules rehearsals and coordinates cross-team windows.
- Training & Enablement: Solutions Eng (Sofia Petrov) — creates quickstart training and checklists.

Handoff Matrix (one row per service; sample columns shown)
Service name | Current owner | Instrumentation owner | SLO target | Runbook owner | Handoff date | Acceptance status
- inference-api | infra-svc-team | infra-metrics | p99 latency < 300ms, error rate < 0.5% | product-inference | 2026-02-10 | pending validation
- embeddings-worker | embeddings-team | infra-metrics | availability 99.9% monthly | embeddings-eng | 2026-02-18 | scheduled

Detailed Ramp Calendar (Q1 2026)
Week 1–2: Cohort kickoff
- Kickoff workshop: goals, SLO templates, what good looks like.
- Delivery: SLO template populated for each service (owner filled).
Week 3–6: Instrumentation sprint
- Tasks: add metrics (success/failure tags, latency histograms, user-context labels), add alert rules to staging.
- Deliverable: metrics in metrics-store + staging dashboard.
Week 7: Validation and chaos smoke
- Run targeted chaos tests (latency injection, partial cluster kill) in staging. Validate SLO signals and alerts.
Week 8–9: Runbook and playbook drafting
- Create step-by-step runbooks for common P1/P2 scenarios. Include diagnostic queries and quick remediation steps.
Week 10: Handoff rehearsal
- 2-hour war room rehearsal with on-call rotation participants and SRE observers.
Week 11: Formal handoff review
- Readiness checklist: dashboards green, runbook accepted, alerts tuned, rehearsals completed. Sign-off and update ownership tags.

Acceptance Criteria for Handoff (must be all true)
- Required metrics instrumented: latency histogram, success/error counters, request routing tags present.
- Dashboard: team dashboard with top two SLO graphs, alert burn-rate panels, recent incidents feed.
- Runbook: playbook with RCA skeleton, mitigation steps, rollback plan, owners.
- On-call rehearsals: at least one successful war room simulation with on-call responding within SLO targets.
- Post-handoff monitoring: platform SRE observes during first 14 days and provides a short QA report.

Communication & Cadence
- Weekly SLO Sync (30m): update on instrumentation blockers and readiness. Attendees: Program Lead, Instrumentation, Product Owners.
- Bi-weekly Readiness Review (1h): cohort review with SRE leadership for formal approvals.
- Slack channel: #sre-slo (alerts and quick questions), create per-cohort temporary channel for troubleshooting.
- Quarterly scorecard: emailed to Eng + Product leadership summarizing adoption metrics.

On-call and Escalation changes
- Ownership transition: once sign-off done, update on-call rota and PagerDuty escalation policies.
- Escalation policy template: first responder (service team), SRE escalation after 15 minutes for P1, SRE leader after 60 minutes.
- Auto-escalation rules to be implemented by Release & Ops Coordinator during handoff week.

Training & Enablement
- Quickstart play: 2-hour hands-on lab covering metric primitives, dashboarding, and simple runbook creation. Mandatory for product owners before handoff.
- Office hours: weekly drop-in with Observability SME for two months after handoff.
- Living FAQ: add common pitfalls and mitigation notes to the SRE Confluence page at confluence:REL-SLO-RAMP-2026.

Instrumentation checklist (developer-friendly)
- Add histogram for request latency with 10ms buckets up to 5s.
- Increment success and failure counters with user-facing error labels.
- Surface upstream/downstream call durations as separate metrics.
- Emit service and region tags for routing analysis.
- Include a boolean flag or metric for cache-hit vs miss where relevant.

Risk register & mitigations
- Risk: Alert fatigue from noisy early thresholds. Mitigation: staggered alert enablement; start with burn-rate alerts in P0, gate page alerts until validated.
- Risk: Owners lack time for runbook maintenance. Mitigation: agree on quarterly runbook reviews and assign a small recurring 2-hr task in team sprints.
- Risk: Missing key metrics on older services. Mitigation: temporary platform-side adapters to backfill critical signals for the first 14 days post-handoff.

Monitoring & Dashboards (what to check first)
- SLO health panel (daily): error budget remaining, burn-rate, p50/p90/p99 latency.
- Incident velocity panel: count of alerts firing by team in last 7d.
- Recent deploys vs error budget: cross-reference recent releases to sudden burn events.

Go/no-go decision criteria (readiness review)
- All acceptance criteria met.
- No more than one unresolved P1-level instrumentation blocker.
- On-call rota updated and participants confirmed.
- Program Lead and Product Owner approval recorded in the readiness review notes.

Post-handoff runway (14 days)
- SRE observes alerts and provides one improvement ticket (if needed).
- If SLO violations > thresholds for two consecutive days, automatic rollback to pre-handoff alerting and SRE remediation window.

Next steps (immediately actionable)
1) Confirm cohort A services list by 2025-11-07. (Owner: Product leads)
2) Schedule kickoff workshop for 2025-11-12. (Owner: Program Lead)
3) Create per-service starter dashboards using monitoring-configs repo template. (Owner: Instrumentation Engineers)
4) Open JIRA epic ENG-8123 for the first cohort and link service tickets.

Appendix: Quick links and boilerplate text to copy
- SLO template (copyable): SLO name, objective, measurement window, blackout windows, alert rules, on-call contacts.
- Runbook template: symptoms, immediate checks, mitigation steps, escalation matrix, postmortem link.
- Slack snippet for handoff announcement: "Handoff complete: service X — runbook and dashboards available at <link>. On-call rota updated."

Comments/Notes
- This is intentionally prescriptive on the operational steps but lightweight on policy. If product/legal constraints require additional audit trails, we will add a compliance sign-off step to the readiness review.
- Expect refinement after cohort A and incorporate lessons into the SRE playbook.

Signed: 
Maya Chen (Program Lead, Site Reliability Engineering)
